Safari profile behavior vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Safari profile support on device covers storefront language. Profile stores, extension scoping, and Connect actually separate in-app profile behavior from product-page copy:

  • Settings → Safari → Profiles — where buyers create Work, Personal, School, or custom Safari browsing profiles on device. Controls on-device profile separation — not App Store language. AppLocale does not perform this.
  • Profile picker & switch profiles — the Safari UI buyers use to move between browsing contexts. Product-page copy should describe that workflow; building profile-picker UI is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Per-profile Favorites & History — each Safari profile keeps its own bookmark collection and browsing history, distinct from other profiles. Listing copy names that isolation; building profile-scoped data stores is engineering.
  • Per-profile Tab Groups & extensions — tab groups and enabled Safari extensions can differ by profile. zh-Hans overlays should name 标签页组 and extension sets when your English frames show profile-scoped organization — not English-only "Tab Groups" pasted through machine translation.

  • Private Browsing (different surface) — ephemeral session within a profile, not a separate Work/Personal profile container. Related buyer vocabulary but not the same product story — mention only as contrast on profile hero frames.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Safari profile support in the binary.
